kjv: O Lucifer, son of the morning
mine: O Shining One, son of Dawn
note: Hebrew helel ben-shachar "shining one, son of dawn" (the morning star, Venus) is a taunt against the king of Babylon (v. 4). "Lucifer" is the Vulgate's Latin for the morning star; the KJV kept it as a proper name, which fostered its later identification with Satan. Context: Shining One, son of Dawn (taunt on the king of Babylon) (high confidence). Helel ben-shachar 'shining one, son of dawn' names the morning star (Venus), and 14:4 explicitly makes the song a taunt 'against the king of Babylon'. 'Lucifer' is the Vulgate's Latin word for the morning star, not a Hebrew name. Applying the passage to Satan's fall is a later, secondary interpretation. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Lucifer' as a proper name, applied to Satan — Vulgate lucifer, KJV, Tertullian, Origen and much later Christian tradition (cf. Luke 10:18); (2) 'Day Star / morning star' — LXX heosphoros, ESV, NRSV, NIV, NASB, CSB; (3) 'Howl!' (helel from yalal, as in Zech 11:2) — Peshitta and some ancient Jewish readers.
Hebrew qippod is probably the hedgehog or porcupine (cf. Arabic qunfudh), though some take it as a bird.
Hebrew tsepha' is a venomous snake (viper); the "cockatrice" was a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg.
